I'm fairly sure US law is similar to UK law in this respect. In the UK, trade mark infringement wouldn't cover this because it only protects a mark within a specified class or classes in which your business operates. Unless GameStop was in the food business and registered its trade mark to cover it, it's fair game for anyone else to copy aspects of their mark. There's a separate claim in "passing off" if you're likely to cause confusion amongst customers that your product originates from someone else. Unless a reasonable person looks at that sign and thinks, "Oh, GameStop has a burger outlet!" there's no passing off. That likely would stop someone using both the GameStop name and logo for another unrelated business even where they have not registered the mark.
